data.note:
Note: unblinded as Epithelial (internal code AZ-J, no PubChem structure or ChEMBL mechanism). My call Protein synthesis was wrong.

What misled me: NSC vote was 4/4 for Protein synthesis across doses, which I used as prior. Similarities were modest (~0.57-0.61, 0.23 at low dose) and k-list was split Protein synthesis / Eg5 inhibitors, so evidence was weak. The strong frac_multinucleate_proxy + eccentricity + shrinking nuc_area looked dose-dependent, but both microscopist reports flagged crowding/touching nuclei in compact colonies vs true multinucleation, intact tubulin/actin, and no mitotic arrest - more consistent with Epithelial colony compaction which I kept at only 0.08.

Lesson: down-weight NSC when similarity low and split, and up-weight visual crowding artifact + Epithelial morphology signals.

Literature searches for phenotype context returned 0 hits, so no PMIDs to cite.

reflection.text:
I concluded Protein synthesis at p=0.60 because all 4 acquired wells voted Protein synthesis by 1-NN NSC and showed dose-dependent nuclear shrinkage with intact tubulin/actin. That followed the protocol prior, but the unblinding shows truth was Epithelial, so the atlas vote itself was wrong for AZ-J.

I was misled by e5/e9 NSC 4/4 and by the very large z-scores for frac_multinucleate_proxy (+10.9, +9.0, +8.0) and nuc_eccentricity (+7.7, +7.9) in e2/e3/e8, which I read as a specific protein-synthesis-like shrinkage/elongation signature with rising tub_mean and nuc_dna_mean. I underweighted warning signs: per-well similarities were modest (0.608, 0.571, 0.612 and 0.226 at 0.1 uM), k-neighbours were split Protein synthesis 5/10 vs Eg5 inhibitors 5/10 then 4/10, dose_response for the top feature was weak (rho=+0.40, p=0.6), and the microscopist flagged lower density and later suggested Aurora kinase inhibitors.

The error was an acquisition and weighting choice: I acquired four doses (1, 10, 0.1, 0.3 uM) as single reps with no replicate or sparse-seed density control, then locked on NSC despite keeping Epithelial at 0.15 then 0.08. I should have treated the multinucleate-proxy signal as potentially artifactual crowding/adhesion rather than confirmatory of translation inhibition.
what_was_right: Detected a strong, reproducible shape phenotype: high frac_multinucleate_proxy and nuc_eccentricity with reduced nuc_major_axis across 1, 10 and 0.3 uM (e2, e3, e8).
Correctly ruled against microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers and actin disruptors on visual grounds of intact cytoskeleton in e4/e17.

Flagged dose-dependent nuclear area shrinkage (rho=-1.00) and eccentricity increase (rho=+1.00) with weak/no mitotic arrest signal, which argued against classic Eg5/Aurora arrest even though neighbours suggested them.
what_was_wrong: Overweighted compare_to_reference_atlas NSC 4/4 (e5, e9) despite low per-well similarity including 0.226 and a 5/5 split with Eg5 inhibitors in k-neighbours, treating an ambiguous neighbourhood as confident.

Misinterpreted frac_multinucleate_proxy and frac_large_nucleus elevations as supporting protein synthesis while discounting microscopist density-lower observation and second call of Aurora kinase inhibitors in e17.

Kept Epithelial in hypotheses (0.15 to 0.08) but never tested it: no sparse-density replating, no adhesion/cytoskeletal junction readouts, and no translation assay to falsify protein synthesis; four single-rep wells could not separate crowding artifact from true cytokinesis failure.
reflection.next_experiment: Re-plate at low/sparse density with DMSO density-matched controls plus OPP-puromycylation translation assay and E-cadherin / actin cell-cell adhesion imaging to directly test protein synthesis vs epithelial/adhesion mechanism and whether multinucleate-proxy and eccentricity signals were crowding artifacts.

## Reflection

I concluded Protein synthesis at p=0.60 because all 4 acquired wells voted Protein synthesis by 1-NN NSC and showed dose-dependent nuclear shrinkage with intact tubulin/actin. That followed the protocol prior, but the unblinding shows truth was Epithelial, so the atlas vote itself was wrong for AZ-J.

I was misled by e5/e9 NSC 4/4 and by the very large z-scores for frac_multinucleate_proxy (+10.9, +9.0, +8.0) and nuc_eccentricity (+7.7, +7.9) in e2/e3/e8, which I read as a specific protein-synthesis-like shrinkage/elongation signature with rising tub_mean and nuc_dna_mean. I underweighted warning signs: per-well similarities were modest (0.608, 0.571, 0.612 and 0.226 at 0.1 uM), k-neighbours were split Protein synthesis 5/10 vs Eg5 inhibitors 5/10 then 4/10, dose_response for the top feature was weak (rho=+0.40, p=0.6), and the microscopist flagged lower density and later suggested Aurora kinase inhibitors.

The error was an acquisition and weighting choice: I acquired four doses (1, 10, 0.1, 0.3 uM) as single reps with no replicate or sparse-seed density control, then locked on NSC despite keeping Epithelial at 0.15 then 0.08. I should have treated the multinucleate-proxy signal as potentially artifactual crowding/adhesion rather than confirmatory of translation inhibition.

What was right:
- Detected a strong, reproducible shape phenotype: high frac_multinucleate_proxy and nuc_eccentricity with reduced nuc_major_axis across 1, 10 and 0.3 uM (e2, e3, e8).
- Correctly ruled against microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers and actin disruptors on visual grounds of intact cytoskeleton in e4/e17.
- Flagged dose-dependent nuclear area shrinkage (rho=-1.00) and eccentricity increase (rho=+1.00) with weak/no mitotic arrest signal, which argued against classic Eg5/Aurora arrest even though neighbours suggested them.

What was wrong or missed:
- Overweighted compare_to_reference_atlas NSC 4/4 (e5, e9) despite low per-well similarity including 0.226 and a 5/5 split with Eg5 inhibitors in k-neighbours, treating an ambiguous neighbourhood as confident.
- Misinterpreted frac_multinucleate_proxy and frac_large_nucleus elevations as supporting protein synthesis while discounting microscopist density-lower observation and second call of Aurora kinase inhibitors in e17.
- Kept Epithelial in hypotheses (0.15 to 0.08) but never tested it: no sparse-density replating, no adhesion/cytoskeletal junction readouts, and no translation assay to falsify protein synthesis; four single-rep wells could not separate crowding artifact from true cytokinesis failure.

Proposed next experiment: Re-plate at low/sparse density with DMSO density-matched controls plus OPP-puromycylation translation assay and E-cadherin / actin cell-cell adhesion imaging to directly test protein synthesis vs epithelial/adhesion mechanism and whether multinucleate-proxy and eccentricity signals were crowding artifacts.
